messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: axis.text.x (for facets)
parts:
Hi there,

I wanted to enlarge all text-setting by modifying the base_size of the
theme but I realized that it does not seem to work if I use facets:

df <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 10:1, z = rep(c("cat1","cat2"),5))

# small text, no facets
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 8))
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point()

# large text, no facets
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 18))
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point()

# small text, facets
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 8))
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap( ~ z)

# large text, facets DOES NOT WORK
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 18))
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap( ~ z)

# even this does not work
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap( ~ z) +
opts(axis.text.x <- theme_text(size = 18, colour = "red", angle = 90))

What is wrong with my code???

Antje

messages.author: e715a3aeb27b07f3
messages.subject: Re: axis.text.x (for facets)
parts:
I've managed to reproduce the problem. It appears when I change the
angle for the x axis like this:
p <- p + opts(axis.text.x <- theme_text(angle = 90)

This overwrites any size given by the theme setting (theme_text
default size is "10").

Kohske provided my a little workaround to set the angle without
loosing my size settings:

tm <- theme_bw(base_size=12)
formals(tm$axis.text.x)$angle <- 90
qplot(1:10, 1:10) + tm


Maybe it helps someone else :-)

Antje
